ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure are two terminals, and between the terminals is marked a direction arrow of voltage U; starting from the upper terminal along the upper wire, there is a direction arrow of current I, then resistor R is connected in sequence; the right vertical branch is marked with inductive impedance jX_L; the bottom branch connects capacitive impedance, marked as -jX_C, and returns to the lower-left terminal. Therefore the figure shows R, jX_L, and -jX_C connected in series in the same loop, and the same current I flows through each element. Reasoning: The total impedance of a series circuit is the sum of each impedance: Z_total = R + jX_L - jX_C = R + j(X_L - X_C). Its impedance magnitude is |Z_total| = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2). By Ohm's law in phasor form, the current magnitude I = U / |Z_total|, so I = U / sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2).
